note: Corpus v0: vendored public repos only. Contrastive pairs and scenario configs are authored in S2, after the taxonomy exists.

terragoat.scope_note: AWS only. alicloud/azure/gcp/oracle omitted - they add rule volume, not category coverage.

cases.note: Reconciled against upstream at this pin: there is no vpc.tf. elb.tf is the only networking-only file (aws_elb, plain HTTP listener on lb_port 80). The rest of the networking footprint is split across ec2.tf (aws_vpc, aws_subnet x2, aws_internet_gateway, aws_route_table, aws_route, aws_route_table_association x2, aws_network_interface, aws_security_group, aws_flow_log) and db-app.tf (aws_security_group, aws_security_group_rule x2).

aws_instance, aws_ebs_volume, aws_ebs_snapshot, aws_volume_attachment. Upstream co-locates the VPC, subnet, route-table and security-group resources in this same file instead of a separate vpc.tf, so this file also carries most of the networking footprint.

A directory, not a file: 24 files across 15 scenario directories. 16 are plain Kubernetes manifests (Deployment, Job, ClusterRole/RoleBinding, Kyverno policy); the other 8 are the metadata-db Helm chart (Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/) whose Go template syntax a plain YAML parser cannot read. Helm is in conceptual scope but not the evaluation focus.
